newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude holds firmer trend, Urals steady.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude holds firmer trend, Urals steady.

text.p: North Sea crudes were slightly firmer in early trade on Friday, buoyed by increasing refinery demand, traders said.
But in the cash market, June Brent slipped a little, trading three cents a barrel down at $18.38 by 1215 GMT.
Traders said the IPE June contract was pushed lower by some selling from players trying to test the downside, adding there was no fundamental news behind the slip.
The Brent physical market was quiet but two cargoes of Norwegian Oseberg loading May 17-19 and May 19-21 changed hands on Friday at Dated Brent +15 cents and +13 cents respectively.
This was about seven cents higher than its last level.
"The market is picking up...due to increasing demand from end users," one Norwegian trader said.
Traders said other North Sea grades also looked good, talked at last traded levels, Statfjord at Dated Brent +13 to +15 cents and Ekofisk at a 20-cent premium to Dated Brent.
On the paper market, one outright June contract exchanged hands at $18.54.
Four Brent cargoes were due to turn wet on Friday, one loading May 10-12, one May 11-13 and two May 12-14, traders said.
One trader said the U.S. Gulf market for crude "is looking a little bit healthier but I can't tell you that I have heard anything specific (going there)".

"I think there is slightly more positive sentiment out there...I think we slipped from an uncertainty over how much demand there was going to be for May to sellers now seeing better demand," one trader said.
Brent intermonth spreads firmed slightly, with May/June talked at -18/-12, three cents above Thursday's level, while Jun/Jul and Jul/Aug were one to two cents stronger than a day before.
Brent CFDs were little changed, next week's dates talked at June Brent -39/-30 cents and May 5-9 at June Brent -34/-28.

In a quiet Mediterranean market, Russian Urals held steady but traders said they would face competition from cheaper sour grades soon. They said at least two Urals cargoes for early May loading were on offer in the Dated Brent -$1.10/-$1.00 range.

"Certainly Kirkuk looks good value compared to Urals at that kind of price but the people that are selling the Kirkuk are taking most of the value out of it by charging large premiums," one trader said.
"There's still quite a lot of unsold April Kirkuk available...and there's also a few boats of Iranian Heavy floating around as well, again which is going to be competitive with Urals," she said.
